items.question:
A UX researcher at an e-commerce platform has tried three different single-variable prompt changes for thematic analysis of interview transcripts. All three iterations produce similar poor results: themes are too broad and sub-themes are consistently missed. She is considering making multiple changes simultaneously in the next attempt.

In what circumstance would testing multiple changes simultaneously be MOST justified?

options.A: When multiple single-variable iterations have converged on the same failure, suggesting the entire approach needs rethinking rather than incremental adjustment.
options.B: When the project deadline is approaching and there is no time for sequential iteration.
options.C: When each individual change is small and unlikely to have a measurable independent effect.
options.D: When the practitioner is experienced enough with the tool to reliably predict which combination will succeed.

items.question:
A brand manager at a pharmaceutical company asks Claude to analyse whether three of the company's pipeline compounds would qualify for FDA Fast Track designation. The output is shallow and contains factually inaccurate statements about key designation criteria. The brand manager's regulatory affairs colleagues dismiss the analysis.

Is this MOST likely a poor-fit issue or a prompt problem?

options.A: Poor fit — Claude lacks sufficient knowledge of FDA Fast Track designation criteria to produce reliable analysis.
options.B: Likely a prompt problem — the analysis needs the designation criteria and compound-specific data explicitly provided; a structured prompt with that context would likely produce substantially better output.
options.C: Poor fit — FDA regulatory analysis requires formal legal opinion by a licensed regulatory attorney, outside Claude's scope.
options.D: Likely a prompt problem — switching to the highest-reasoning tier would produce more accurate regulatory analysis.

items.question:
A knowledge manager at a management consultancy has spent three weeks trying to get Claude to produce reliably consistent topic tagging across 5,000 consulting reports (one at a time). Despite explicit taxonomies, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought prompting, and testing across lightweight, mid, and high-reasoning tiers, approximately 18% of tags are inconsistently applied in unpredictable ways. No prompt pattern predicts where errors will occur.

What does this pattern MOST likely indicate?

options.A: The prompt taxonomy has an internal ambiguity that causes inconsistent application regardless of tier or prompt quality.
options.B: The corpus of 5,000 reports is too large for Claude to handle with reliable single-pass consistency.
options.C: This use case warrants deterministic tagging logic or a purpose-built classification tool, not continued prompt iteration.
options.D: Batch processing the reports would resolve the consistency issue by standardising inference conditions.

items.question: A policy director at a public health agency has maintained a single Claude conversation for three months developing a national immunisation framework. Two problems have appeared: (1) recent outputs reference scientific consensus framing from early in the thread rather than more recent evidence she added in later turns; and (2) formatting has diverged from the structured section headings she specified at the start. (Choose TWO statements that MOST accurately explain these failure modes.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: The early scientific framing is more prominent in the model's attention than the later evidence additions because early content established the narrative frame, and in a very long thread, that frame persists even when later evidence should update it.
options.B: Claude is actively learning from which references the policy director engaged with most, creating a reinforcement bias toward early-thread sources.
options.C: Format instructions are lost because Claude's session memory does not retain structural specifications beyond a configurable turn limit.
options.D: The heading specifications from the beginning of the thread are diluted by hundreds of subsequent turns, reducing their influence on current formatting decisions.
options.E: Both failures indicate the scientific content has exceeded Claude's domain knowledge in immunisation policy.

items.question: A content team at a media streaming company has saved its best Claude prompts in a shared Google Doc. Three months in, two problems emerge: (A) prompts that worked well are now producing lower-quality results as content needs evolve; (B) new team members cannot determine which prompt version is current or which produced the best results for which content type. (Choose TWO actions that would MOST effectively address BOTH problems.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: Archive old prompt versions in a separate folder to reduce clutter in the shared document.
options.B: Establish a versioned prompt library with documented performance results, success criteria, and content-type mapping for each prompt.
options.C: Ask Claude to recommend improvements to each template based on current content needs at regular intervals.
options.D: Assign a named prompt owner for each content type who is responsible for keeping their prompt current.
options.E: Move the prompt templates into a Claude Project as custom instructions with version notes embedded, so current prompts load automatically for the relevant content type.

items.question: An analytics head at a retail bank has implemented three cost optimisations: all tasks on the lightweight tier (65% cost saving), system prompts trimmed to 200 tokens (20% input saving), and maximum output capped at 500 tokens across all calls. Analysts report credit risk summaries are too brief for decision support, complex structured product analysis is unreliable, and some regulatory report sections are cut off mid-paragraph. (Choose TWO root causes that MOST explain these problems collectively.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: The universal lightweight-tier routing has removed the reasoning depth required for complex credit risk and structured product analysis.
options.B: A 200-token system prompt is too short to express full task instructions, causing Claude to fill gaps with assumptions.
options.C: The 500-token output cap is insufficient for the length required by credit risk summaries and regulatory sections, causing premature truncation.
options.D: A 65% cost reduction indicates over-optimisation; costs should not be reduced by more than 40% to preserve quality.
options.E: The lightweight tier cannot process structured financial data; quantitative analysis requires a higher-reasoning tier.

items.question: A claims adjuster at a general insurance company correctly opens a new Claude conversation for each claim to maintain context isolation. However, two friction points emerge: she must re-paste the standard claims assessment framework into every new conversation; and she cannot easily compare how Claude assessed similar loss events across different conversations. (Choose TWO structural improvements that address BOTH friction points most effectively.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: Merge all claim conversations into a single running thread to enable direct cross-claim comparison.
options.B: Move the standard claims assessment framework to a Project instruction so it loads automatically in every new conversation.
options.C: Copy the prior claim's analysis into the opening message of each new conversation as a style and context anchor.
options.D: Use a structured claim summary template to record key findings from each conversation in a shared document, enabling cross-claim comparison outside of Claude.
options.E: Ask Claude at the end of each conversation to generate a comparison-ready summary formatted for cross-claim analysis.

items.question:
A compliance technology lead at a wealth management firm has spent six weeks deploying Claude for automated draft review of investment suitability letters. After extensive prompt engineering across all tiers, two failures persist: (1) approximately 5% of letters have product risk profiles inverted (high-risk described as conservative); (2) the errors are semantically plausible and grammatically correct, making them undetectable without independent verification. IT has confirmed no technical issues.

What should he do NEXT?

options.A: Set a lower temperature on API calls to reduce probabilistic variation in risk profile assignments.
options.B: Add a self-validation step asking Claude to cross-check its own risk profile assignments against a supplied reference list.
options.C: File a detailed defect report with Anthropic documenting the systematic inversion pattern for investigation.
options.D: Redesign the workflow so a human reviewer validates risk profile assignments before each letter is finalised, and treat Claude as a drafting assistant rather than an autonomous reviewer for this element.

items.question:
A bid writer at a 200-person professional services firm is producing a proposal methodology section in a 60-turn conversation. He requests a 10-section overview. Sections 1–5 are correct; section 6 refers to a different client's scope that was discussed in earlier turns of this thread; section 7 ends mid-sentence.

Which statement BEST describes the set of problems present?

options.A: Both conversation drift (wrong client reference in section 6) and output truncation (mid-sentence ending in section 7) are present simultaneously.
options.B: Only truncation is present; the wrong client reference in section 6 is a knowledge gap about this specific client.
options.C: Only conversation drift is present; the mid-sentence ending in section 7 is intentional because Claude detected the section was off-topic.
options.D: The wrong client reference is a refusal signal, while the mid-sentence ending is caused by truncation.

items.question:
A customer insights analyst at a retail bank has spent four hours in a Claude conversation building a customer segmentation framework — now 80 turns long. Quality has been degrading for the last 20 turns. Her manager asks whether it is more cost-effective to continue fixing the current output or to start fresh.

Which framing MOST accurately guides this decision?

options.A: The time already invested in the current thread is a sunk cost; the decision should be based purely on future expected time, ignoring the history.
options.B: Starting fresh is more cost-effective if creating a structured briefing and completing the work in a new conversation will take less total time than correcting the degraded output in the existing thread.
options.C: Continuing is always more cost-effective because the existing context eliminates the need to re-establish any information.
options.D: Restarting is only warranted when the thread has completely failed, not when it has merely degraded.

items.question:
A portfolio manager at a 12-person investment boutique has a high-performing Claude prompt template for quarterly investment committee reports — built over six months. The firm is adding three new analysts. The CIO wants consistent, reliable access to the template across the growing team.

What structural change would MOST effectively standardise and scale the prompt?

options.A: Share the document with all analysts and ask each to copy the prompt manually into their conversations.
options.B: Train all analysts on the prompt wording so they can reproduce it from memory during report production.
options.C: Move the template to a shared Claude Project as custom instructions so it loads automatically for every team member accessing the Project.
options.D: Ask Claude to generate a simplified version of the template that requires less expertise to use correctly.

items.question:
A documentation specialist at a pharmaceutical company uploads an 80-page process validation protocol and asks Claude to identify all decision points and approval gates. Claude identifies 12, but she knows from direct familiarity that at least 18 exist. The gaps appear concentrated in pages 35–55.

What two-step approach would MOST reliably produce a complete list?

options.A: Ask Claude to repeat the analysis with emphasis on locating 'all decision points, including minor ones.'
options.B: Upload only pages 35–55 in a separate conversation and ask for decision points within that section only.
options.C: Switch to the highest-reasoning tier and rerun the full document analysis to capture what was missed.
options.D: Note the 12 already identified and send a targeted follow-up: review pages 35–55 specifically and add any decision points not included in the prior list.

items.question:
An information governance manager at a healthcare system reports two Claude-related problems from this week: (Problem 1) a patient data classification API produces different labels on identical inputs in different runs; (Problem 2) a compliance recommendation output suggested deleting all patient data after 30 days, contradicting all applicable retention regulations.

Which assessment correctly characterises BOTH problems?

options.A: Problem 1 is expected probabilistic behaviour managed through prompt engineering; Problem 2 is a poor-fit signal — compliance recommendations require expert validation before any action is taken.
options.B: Problem 1 is a technical defect requiring IT escalation; Problem 2 is a prompt problem that better instructions would prevent.
options.C: Both problems require IT escalation: Problem 1 is a server-side consistency failure and Problem 2 indicates a safety filter bypass.
options.D: Problem 1 is a model capability limitation making classification unsuitable; Problem 2 is expected since compliance guidance is inherently uncertain.

items.question:
A content operations manager at a media company has been iterating a Claude prompt for 5 days, now on version 9. Versions 3–7 improved steadily. Version 7 was the clearest success. Versions 8 and 9 underperform version 7 in measurable ways.

What is the MOST appropriate next step?

options.A: Continue from version 9 with one more targeted change and see if the downward trend reverses.
options.B: Return to version 7 as the validated baseline and apply one targeted change from that known-good starting point.
options.C: Discard all nine versions and restart with a fundamentally different prompt structure.
options.D: Run versions 7, 8, and 9 in parallel on fresh test cases to establish which performs best before deciding.

items.question:
An AI program manager at a fintech company is designing a loan document classification system. Three requirements must all be met: (1) misclassification rate below 2% (quality); (2) response time under 3 seconds (latency); (3) monthly cost within the allocated budget. She must select the tier and configuration.

In what ORDER should she evaluate these constraints?

options.A: Cost first — it limits the available options and eliminates tiers that exceed budget before testing anything else.
options.B: Latency first — it is the customer-facing requirement and determines which tiers are technically viable.
options.C: Quality first to establish the minimum acceptable tier, then latency to confirm speed requirements are met, then cost to optimise within the qualified set.
options.D: Run all three evaluations simultaneously in a single pilot to identify the Pareto-optimal configuration.

items.question:
A legal technology manager at a global law firm has 12 active Claude conversations for different practice group templates — each 3–6 months old and several hundred turns long. An audit reveals quality has degraded across all 12. An analysis shows: fresh-starting each conversation (structured briefing + rebuild) would take 6–8 hours per conversation; continuing to remediate each in-thread would take 15–20 hours per conversation.

Which decision BEST weighs the economics and quality risks?

options.A: Continue remediating all 12 in-thread — the existing context contains more institutional value than a fresh start could replicate.
options.B: Fresh-start the two highest-priority conversations immediately; remediate the other 10 in-thread to manage the transition workload.
options.C: Fresh-start only conversations that have completely failed; remediate the others in-thread to preserve their development history.
options.D: Fresh-start all 12 with proper briefings — the 6–8 hour investment per conversation is significantly more efficient than 15–20 hours of in-thread remediation and produces higher-quality output from a clean context.

items.question:
A trade compliance officer at a manufacturing company asks Claude to determine the correct HTS tariff code for a specific machine component under recently updated trade regulations. Claude produces a confident, detailed classification analysis. An external trade attorney reviews it and identifies two material errors in the regulatory interpretation.

Which assessment MOST accurately diagnoses this situation?

options.A: This is primarily a task-fit issue — HTS classification is a specialised legal determination that requires expert review; Claude's output should have been treated as a draft for attorney validation, not as a final determination.
options.B: This is a prompt problem — including the specific regulation text would allow Claude to produce accurate HTS classifications reliably.
options.C: This is a technical problem — the errors indicate a model inconsistency that should be documented and escalated to IT.
options.D: This is a knowledge cutoff issue — recent trade regulation updates were not reflected because of the model's training data limitations.

items.question:
A workforce analytics manager at a large enterprise is designing a Claude-based workflow for weekly employee retention risk reports. She needs: (1) consistent methodology across her 5-person team; (2) continuity of approach across weekly sessions; (3) the ability to refine the approach over time without losing what works.

Which combination of practices MOST effectively addresses all three goals?

options.A: Maintain one long-running team conversation with a protocol for adding new turns each week.
options.B: Create a shared Project with the methodology as custom instructions, start a fresh conversation for each report, and maintain a versioned prompt log documenting improvements and results.
options.C: Use the same chat for each weekly report, saving the full conversation history as a backup.
options.D: Assign one analyst as the sole prompt maintainer and have others submit report requests through that person for consistency.

items.question:
A research director at a market research firm has been trying for three weeks to get Claude to analyse proprietary survey data with non-standard column headers and merged cells. Outputs are generic and ignore most data fields. She is preparing to conclude that Claude is fundamentally incapable of analysing her data format and abandon the workflow.

Before accepting this conclusion, what should she verify FIRST?

options.A: Whether the survey data format falls within Claude's documented data analysis capabilities for proprietary formats.
options.B: Whether switching to the highest-reasoning tier would produce better analysis of the custom headers and merged cells.
options.C: Whether the file is being correctly parsed as readable text and whether the non-standard headers and merged cells are rendering correctly when processed.
options.D: Whether the prompt includes sufficient examples of the expected analysis output format.

items.question:
To reduce API costs, an IT team at an insurance company sets the maximum output token limit to 300 on the compliance team's Claude integration. Monthly costs drop. However, compliance analysts begin submitting partial audit checklists to regulators — the checklists are routinely cut off before completion by the token limit.

What does this situation MOST clearly illustrate?

options.A: The compliance team should switch to a cheaper model tier as an alternative to restricting output length.
options.B: Output token limits should be set by business users, not by IT teams.
options.C: 300 tokens is below the minimum supported output limit for compliance applications.
options.D: Cost optimisation applied without testing against task requirements can create serious downstream compliance failures.

items.question:
An environmental consultant at an engineering firm uploads a 50-page environmental impact assessment and asks Claude to summarise all regulatory obligations. The summary covers sections 1–15 and 40–50, but appears to omit the middle sections entirely. The response also ends mid-sentence before completing the summary for section 40–50.

What combined set of actions should she take NEXT?

options.A: First, send a continuation prompt in the same thread to complete the truncated portion; second, send a targeted follow-up asking Claude to review sections 16–39 for regulatory obligations not yet captured.
options.B: Start a new conversation and resubmit the entire document with an instruction to pay special attention to the middle sections.
options.C: Switch to a higher-tier model and rerun the full analysis to address both the truncation and the middle-section gaps simultaneously.
options.D: Ask Claude to re-read its own response and identify what it omitted from the middle sections.

items.question:
A customer experience director at a 150-property hospitality chain is optimising a guest feedback analysis pipeline. Currently: mid-tier model, 2,000-token prompts, 600-token outputs, 5-second response time, 90% accuracy. Requirements: reduce cost by 30%, maintain 90% accuracy, keep response time under 3 seconds. Analysis: switching to lightweight tier → accuracy 82%; capping output at 300 tokens → accuracy 85%; trimming prompt to 800 tokens → accuracy 88%. No single option meets all three requirements.

What does this analysis MOST clearly indicate?

options.A: She should trim the prompt to 800 tokens as it has the smallest accuracy impact and is closest to meeting all three requirements.
options.B: No single optimisation lever achieves all three constraints; she should either relax the accuracy requirement or explore approaches that reduce cost differently, such as prompt caching or query segmentation.
options.C: She should accept the lightweight tier because an 82% accuracy rate is within acceptable range for a hospitality feedback use case.
options.D: She should reduce output to 300 tokens as the 5% accuracy trade-off is the smallest proportional loss relative to the cost saving achieved.

items.question:
A process improvement lead at a manufacturing conglomerate has been iterating a Claude prompt for defect root cause classification for six weeks across 12 prompt versions. He changed multiple variables simultaneously on several iterations and did not record which changes drove improvements. He now cannot determine whether he is near a capability ceiling or has simply lost track of his best version.

What does this situation MOST illustrate, and what should he do FIRST?

options.A: He has hit a model capability ceiling; he should escalate to IT to assess whether a purpose-built fine-tuned classifier is available.
options.B: He has been iterating too slowly; he should make simultaneous changes to the remaining variables to accelerate resolution.
options.C: Poor iteration discipline made it impossible to attribute outcomes; he should reconstruct the best-performing version he can recall and restart with documented one-variable iteration from that baseline.
options.D: He should file a support ticket to determine what accuracy rate is achievable for his classification task.

items.question: A solutions architect at a SaaS company is advising a client on two separate decisions: (Decision 1) a 90-turn conversation that has been drifting for 30 turns now needs to produce a high-stakes product requirements document; (Decision 2) the client's API integration costs 20% more than expected because the system prompt was accidentally duplicated in the code. (Choose TWO statements that correctly prescribe the action for each decision.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: For Decision 1: start a fresh conversation with a structured briefing before generating the high-stakes requirements document.
options.B: For Decision 1: continue in the existing thread but consolidate all key requirements into the current prompt to counteract drift.
options.C: For Decision 1: switch to the highest-reasoning tier to compensate for quality lost to context drift.
options.D: For Decision 2: remove the duplicated system prompt content — this is a configuration fix with an immediate cost impact and no quality tradeoff.
options.E: For Decision 2: accept the 20% cost increase as evidence that the system prompt needs to be longer to perform well.

items.question: A digital health officer at an NHS trust is designing a Claude-based clinical documentation support tool. Clinical governance requires every response to include a full explanation (minimum 250 tokens). IT has set a fixed monthly cost ceiling. Current projections show costs will exceed the ceiling by 35% under these constraints. (Choose TWO approaches that MOST effectively reduce cost while preserving the 250-token minimum.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: Reduce the explanation requirement to 150 tokens to bring costs within budget.
options.B: Route only clinical documentation tasks through Claude; handle simpler lookup tasks via a dedicated, cheaper tool.
options.C: Switch to the lightweight tier for all clinical documentation tasks to reduce per-token cost.
options.D: Restrict access to the tool to a subset of staff until costs are better understood.
options.E: Apply prompt caching to the stable clinical guidelines section of the system prompt, which is identical on every call.

items.question: A strategic sourcing manager at a pharmaceutical company has two active problems: (Problem A) an 8-week sourcing strategy conversation has twice recommended supplier categories she explicitly ruled out in week 1 — the errors occur unpredictably and cannot be reproduced on demand; (Problem B) her API integration returns occasional HTTP 500 errors on complex multi-document queries, infrequent and unpredictable. (Choose TWO actions that correctly address each problem.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: For Problem A: extract the governing supplier criteria into a structured briefing and use fresh conversations going forward — the 8-week drift makes in-thread correction unreliable.
options.B: For Problem A: escalate to IT — unpredictable recommendation errors in a long conversation thread indicate a server-side model defect.
options.C: For Problem B: log the error patterns (timestamp, query type, HTTP error code) and escalate to IT with that documented evidence.
options.D: For Problem B: accept the occasional 500 errors as normal API variability and implement a client-side retry mechanism without escalation.
options.E: For Problem A: add the excluded supplier categories as an explicit exclusion list to the top of every future prompt in the existing thread.

items.question: A talent acquisition manager at a professional services firm runs a Claude-powered job description and screening workflow. Two ongoing problems: (1) job description quality is declining as the shared conversation thread grows and team members add turns inconsistently; (2) a high-performing candidate assessment framework was developed two months ago and is now buried in old chat history that the team cannot locate. (Choose TWO structural changes that address BOTH problems.) (Choose TWO)

options.A: Assign one team member to manage all Claude interactions to enforce consistency and maintain access to past discoveries.
options.B: Move the job description methodology to a Claude Project with custom instructions, and start a new conversation for each job requisition.
options.C: Use separate Claude accounts for each team member to prevent cross-contamination of conversation threads.
options.D: Extract the candidate assessment framework from the old conversation and document it in a shared knowledge base, then add its core principles to the Project instructions for automatic loading.
options.E: Ask Claude to retrieve the assessment framework from its memory of the original conversation that developed it.

items.question:
A chief of staff at a 400-person logistics company has used a single Claude conversation for 4 months for competitive intelligence and board-level strategy summaries. Problems have accumulated: (1) recent summaries reference competitors that have exited the market — possibly drift or knowledge cutoff; (2) a market entry recommendation contradicts a risk decision explicitly made in month 1; (3) IT has reported occasional API authentication errors. He must decide how to proceed.

What should he do NEXT?

options.A: File an IT escalation for the authentication errors immediately — technical failures take priority over content quality issues.
options.B: Start a fresh conversation for the strategy summaries immediately, which will resolve all three problems in one action.
options.C: Ask Claude to review all summaries since month 1 and self-identify where it began referencing discontinued competitors.
options.D: Separate the technical issue (authentication errors → flag to IT) from the conversation quality issues (context drift → extract governing decisions, start fresh), addressing each through its correct channel simultaneously.

items.question: A financial analyst at a 200-person wealth management firm wants to use Claude to help with daily work. Which task represents the HIGHEST fit for Claude assistance?

options.A: Summarising each morning's 12 financial news articles into a 3-sentence brief for the team
options.B: Approving or rejecting client investment suitability determinations
options.C: Deciding the allocation percentages in a new model portfolio the firm will launch
options.D: Forecasting equity prices for the firm's proprietary trading desk

items.question: An HR manager at a 4,000-person logistics company receives approximately 800 job applications per month across 40 open roles. She is considering Claude assistance for initial screening. Which factor MOST strongly indicates this volume is a good fit?

options.A: The company already uses an applicant-tracking system that stores all applications in one database
options.B: The screening task repeats in a consistent structure — same fields, same evaluation criteria, same output format — across every application
options.C: The HR team has previously used Claude for drafting job descriptions and found it helpful
options.D: The company's legal counsel has confirmed that automated screening does not violate equal-opportunity laws

items.question: A process improvement manager at a 600-person auto-parts manufacturer is integrating Claude into the shift-handover documentation workflow. Supervisors currently dictate a verbal summary that a technician types up — a 30-minute task done three times per day. Which step represents the BEST fit for Claude assistance?

options.A: Deciding which maintenance issues are critical enough to escalate to the plant manager
options.B: Verifying that machinery readings in the handover match the sensor log in the SCADA system
options.C: Transforming the supervisor's raw voice notes into a structured written handover report
options.D: Approving the completed handover document before it is filed in the quality management system

items.question: A freelance marketing consultant produces social media copy, newsletters, and meeting summaries for clients. She is deciding when to use Claude in batch mode versus interactively. For which task is BATCH mode MOST appropriate?

options.A: Drafting a single custom pitch email for a named prospect the client has briefed her on today
options.B: Responding to the client's rapid-fire questions during a live strategy session
options.C: Exploring three different brand-voice directions with the client to get real-time feedback
options.D: Generating 30 social posts for a month-long campaign, all using the same approved hashtags and tone guide

items.question: A compliance officer at a regional hospital network is reviewing AI use proposals. One proposal is to automatically generate final patient grievance determination letters using only Claude's output with no human review. What is the MOST significant reason this specific workflow design should NOT be approved?

options.A: Patient-facing determination letters have direct legal and clinical consequences; straight-through AI generation without human review removes required accountability from a high-stakes individual decision
options.B: Claude may not have access to the hospital's case management system and could not retrieve the relevant patient record
options.C: Determination letters require a consistent format that Claude might not maintain reliably across cases
options.D: The compliance officer's team is not large enough to handle the additional oversight that AI-generated letters would require

items.question: A legal operations manager is designing a matter-opening workflow. The process starts when a client emails a request and ends with a populated matter record in the practice management system. Five steps are identified: (1) extract key fields from the email, (2) check for conflicts of interest against the firm's client database, (3) draft the engagement letter, (4) route the draft to the responsible partner for review and signature, and (5) create the matter record after the signed letter is returned. She has mapped steps 1 and 3 as Claude-assisted. She is now classifying step 2. What should she do NEXT?

options.A: Assign step 2 to Claude, since conflict checking is a text-comparison task Claude can perform against a provided client list
options.B: Classify step 2 as a human-and-system step, because conflict checking carries ethical and legal obligations requiring a formal database query and attorney sign-off
options.C: Skip step 2 in the workflow design and address conflicts informally as they arise
options.D: Ask Claude to design the remainder of the workflow, since it has already helped map the first two steps

items.question: A merchandise buyer at a regional clothing retailer receives supplier catalogues — typically 60–80 pages — before each buying season and spends two hours per catalogue extracting items meeting the store's sizing and price-band criteria. Which characteristic of this task MOST clearly signals it is a strong fit for Claude assistance?

options.A: The catalogues arrive on a predictable quarterly schedule, making it easy to plan when to run Claude
options.B: The buyer is experienced and can quickly review and correct any extraction errors Claude makes
options.C: The extraction criteria are stable — the same size range and price band apply every season — so the same prompt works across all catalogues
options.D: The catalogues are provided as PDFs, a common format Claude can read directly

items.question: An underwriting team at a specialty insurer proposes having Claude read commercial property submission packages (site survey, loss history, financials) and produce a recommended premium range and coverage terms. A senior underwriter raises concerns. Which characterisation is MOST accurate about why this use case has poor fit without redesign?

options.A: Claude cannot process documents that contain images of site surveys, so inputs would need to be converted to text first
options.B: The submission packages vary too much in length for Claude to handle consistently
options.C: Premium recommendations require access to live actuarial pricing tables that Claude cannot retrieve
options.D: The recommendation step requires expert judgment built from years of underwriting experience, and the output carries direct financial and contractual consequences

items.question: A regulatory affairs director at a mid-size pharmaceutical company prepares approximately 40 Common Technical Document module summaries per submission, each drawing on 8,000–12,000 words of clinical, nonclinical, and regulatory source material. She wants to use Claude to accelerate this work. Which workflow design MOST effectively captures Claude's leverage while keeping risk appropriately controlled?

options.A: Use Claude to produce a structured first draft of each summary from the source documents; a qualified regulatory writer reviews, revises, and approves each draft before it enters the submission package
options.B: Use Claude to produce the final summary text; have the director do a single pass review of the complete submission rather than reviewing individual summaries
options.C: Use Claude to identify which source documents are relevant to each module and have writers author the summaries from scratch using Claude's document index
options.D: Use Claude to generate the summaries and have an automated formatting script validate word count and structure before submission

items.question: A procurement officer at a federal agency maps a tender evaluation process. The agency receives approximately 200 supplier responses per RFP, each running 40–80 pages, scored against 12 fixed criteria. The officer is deciding which step must be designated HUMAN-ONLY in the workflow.

options.A: Extracting each supplier's stated delivery timeline from the response documents
options.B: Assigning final weighted scores and ranking the suppliers for contract award recommendation
options.C: Summarising each supplier's technical approach section against the RFP requirements
options.D: Flagging any supplier responses that appear to be missing mandatory appendices

items.question: A curriculum director at an 80-person EdTech startup produces 4 online courses per month, each requiring 12 lesson scripts, 4 assessment items per lesson, and 1 course-level glossary. She is deciding whether the current production volume justifies the effort of designing and testing reusable Claude-assisted templates. What is the MOST accurate basis for her decision?

options.A: If each team member already has Claude access, no template design effort is needed — they can prompt ad hoc
options.B: The team should wait until they reach 10 courses per month before investing in template design
options.C: Four courses per month producing 48 lesson scripts and 192 assessment items is sufficient volume with a stable structure to justify template investment
options.D: Template design is only worthwhile if the director can guarantee the templates will not need updating for at least 12 months

items.question: A VP of Operations at a 3,000-person logistics company is reviewing a proposal to use Claude for freight audit — checking 18,000 carrier invoices per month against contracted rates and flagging discrepancies for recovery, then generating dispute letters. Which TWO properties MOST strongly indicate this workflow is a high fit for Claude assistance? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The detection rules are precisely defined — each discrepancy type has a documented formula and threshold in the rate contract
options.B: The carrier invoices are issued in 14 different formats, requiring format normalisation before processing
options.C: The company's legal team has approved the use of AI-generated dispute letters for carrier communications
options.D: The volume of 18,000 invoices per month makes human-by-human review of every invoice economically unviable
options.E: The freight audit team currently has two senior analysts who can review flagged discrepancies before disputes are filed

items.question: A clinical operations director at a contract research organisation is reviewing AI use policies. A site coordinator proposes using Claude to generate the final eligibility determination for trial participants — inputting screening data and having Claude output "eligible" or "ineligible" with a rationale, with one coordinator reviewing every determination. The director is considering placing this task in the "should not be automated" category even with that review. What is the BEST argument for that classification?

options.A: Patient screening data contains PHI, and routing it through any AI system creates unacceptable data-privacy risk
options.B: Claude's knowledge cutoff means it may not reflect the most current version of the trial protocol
options.C: Site coordinators lack the technical skills to evaluate whether Claude's eligibility rationales are medically accurate
options.D: Clinical trial eligibility is a medical judgment with regulatory accountability; having a human review an AI determination is cognitively different from making the determination independently, and automation bias may cause the reviewer to ratify errors

items.question: A development director at a 25-person environmental non-profit submits 35 grant applications per year, each requiring a tailored narrative, a budget narrative, and funder-specific questions. She is evaluating how to use Claude most effectively. Which represents the BEST use of Claude in BATCH mode for this workflow?

options.A: Running all the budget narrative drafts at the start of each cycle, since these follow a stable structure and can be quality-checked as a set before the narrative work begins
options.B: Generating all 35 full grant applications simultaneously at the start of the year, then having the grant writer edit each one
options.C: Using Claude interactively for each narrative as the grant writer researches the funder, incorporating funder-specific priorities into the draft
options.D: Drafting all 35 funder-specific question responses simultaneously, even though each funder's questions are unknown until the RFP is released

items.question: A management consulting associate is designing a 5-step workflow for a 50-page client diagnostic report: (1) interview synthesis, (2) benchmark research, (3) gap analysis against benchmarks, (4) executive summary drafting, and (5) senior partner review. What is the correct ORDER of these steps?

A product manager at a telecoms company designs a customer-churn workflow: (1) Claude reads a monthly export of 500,000 customer records with 42 attributes and flags high-risk customers, then (2) the retention team calls flagged customers with personalised offers. The product manager is reviewing the design before implementation. Which concern represents the MOST significant design flaw?

options.A: The export file containing 500,000 records may exceed Claude's practical input limits in a single session
options.B: Retention agents will need training on how to interpret Claude's risk flags before making calls
options.C: The workflow skips validation of whether Claude's classification criteria actually predict churn — deploying an unvalidated classifier sends offers based on unknown-quality flags
options.D: Customer records contain PII that requires anonymisation before being passed to Claude

items.question: A digital transformation lead at a large utility company proposes redesigning the monthly regulatory compliance reporting workflow. Currently, 6 analysts each spend 3 days extracting operational data from 4 internal systems and cross-checking totals across 12 mandated report templates. The proposal: Claude generates completed reports from raw data extracts, with one analyst doing a final review. He claims this reduces a 6-person, 3-day effort to a 1-person, half-day task. Which assessment is MOST accurate?

options.A: The proposal is sound because Claude handles structured data formatting well and the volume reduction is clearly achievable
options.B: The proposal is too conservative — Claude could eliminate the analyst review step, reducing to fully automated report generation
options.C: The proposal is impractical because regulatory report templates are proprietary formats that Claude cannot populate directly
options.D: The proposal underestimates risk: replacing 6 analysts' cross-checks with a single reviewer creates a different error profile — automation bias and reduced checking surface — which may not meet the utility's regulatory obligations

items.question: A content operations manager at a digital media company is redesigning the production workflow for a weekly investigative newsletter. Steps include: researching source articles, drafting the narrative, fact-checking claims, copyediting for house style, editorial selection of stories, and publishing via the email platform. Which TWO steps are BEST suited for Claude to assist with as a first-draft or preparation layer? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Fact-checking claims against independent sources
options.B: Drafting the narrative structure and initial prose from the researcher's notes and source summaries
options.C: Copyediting the completed draft for house style, grammar, and consistency
options.D: Making the final editorial judgment about which stories are newsworthy enough to run
options.E: Publishing the newsletter to subscribers via the email delivery platform

items.question: An e-commerce operations director is evaluating 40 internal process tasks to identify strong candidates for Claude assistance. Which TWO properties MOST reliably indicate that a task is a strong candidate? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The task produces the same type of output every time — for example, a product description following a fixed template
options.B: The task requires interpreting product photographs to assess quality defects
options.C: The task handles a volume the current team cannot comfortably absorb manually within the required turnaround time
options.D: The task has been performed by the same specialist for five years and relies on tacit knowledge about supplier relationships
options.E: The task's output goes directly to a regulated financial statement without any human review

items.question: A hotel group operations manager is reviewing AI use proposals across 12 properties. Two colleagues each propose a task for Claude assistance. Which TWO proposed tasks are MOST clearly poor fits for Claude assistance based on task suitability principles? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Drafting standardised responses to common guest complaint emails, using an approved resolution policy document
options.B: Deciding whether to dismiss a guest-facing employee based on a pattern of complaints, without any HR review
options.C: Summarising weekly guest feedback survey responses (approximately 400 per week) into a structured theme report
options.D: Generating personalised medical dietary recommendations for guests based on their stated health conditions, without physician oversight
options.E: Translating the hotel's printed amenity guide from English into four languages using a provided style guide

items.question: A procurement analyst at a government contractor needs to produce 20 vendor risk summaries by end of week. Each summary requires reading a vendor's 30-page due-diligence questionnaire and a 15-page financial statement. He is debating between batch and interactive modes. What is the PRIMARY criterion that should determine his choice?

options.A: Whether Claude can read 30-page documents reliably in a single session
options.B: Whether all 20 vendors' documents are available now or whether he will receive some later in the week
options.C: Whether his manager prefers a consistent output format across all summaries
options.D: Whether the vendor risk summaries will be reviewed by a compliance officer before being filed

items.question: A research operations manager at a market research firm wants to use Claude to assist with coding qualitative interview responses. Her team interviews 200 participants per study, and each interview transcript is 8–12 pages. A colleague argues this is a strong fit because of the high volume. The manager is not convinced. Which factor would MOST undermine the colleague's volume-based argument?

options.A: The transcripts are stored in a proprietary format that requires conversion before Claude can read them
options.B: The coding scheme changes for each study based on the research question, so the same prompt cannot be reused across projects
options.C: The company does not yet have an enterprise Claude plan, only personal accounts for two researchers
options.D: Qualitative coding requires reading between 20 and 200 pages per study, which may stress Claude's context window
